jobs.subject: Omega — réacteur
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one opaque wide landscape environment master for a Mass Effect fighting-stage prototype.
Primary request: reconstruct the exact central reactor chamber of Mass Effect 3: Omega from the supplied original environment artist screenshots, with maximum architectural fidelity. Input image 1 is the authoritative frontal composition. Input image 2 is only corroborating side-view geometry and materials, not a second scene.
Preserve the enormous recessed circular reactor fan at the rear center, paired monumental vertical pillars, the inward diagonal braces flanking the fan, the small stacked control screens at center, the red low central console, and the two short existing staircases up to the side walkways. Keep the yellow railings, their original platform edges, the left and right existing low cover blocks, the pits underneath the walkways, the diagonal near structural frame, the actual asymmetric small details. Do not turn the existing platform into a new continuous floor spanning the pits.
Composition and style: use the same near-front camera direction and camera height as image 1, the same perspective and proportions. Wide cinematic landscape, tightly filling the frame with the environment only. Remove the black portfolio footer and its text from the composition. If fitting a less panoramic canvas requires more foreground, show only a small continuation of the already visible connected metal deck, without changing the chamber structure. Do not enlarge the floor into a new arena, add bridges, change the stairs, or replace the reactor with a glowing energy orb.
Lighting and material invariants: preserve the dark gray and muted rusty steel, subdued red illumination beneath and around the console, the narrow cold blue light on the inner diagonal braces, dark atmospheric depth, fine metal grating and restrained hazy air. Preserve the original dim exposure but keep the existing near platform readable. Detailed real-time 3D game rendering, not painterly, no added architecture.
Output exactly one complete empty stage master. No characters, mechs, weapons, combat effects, HUD, labels, caption, game title, brand mark, borders or collage. Opaque image.

jobs.subject: Bekenstein — propriété de Hock
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one opaque wide landscape environment master for a Mass Effect fighting-stage prototype.
Primary request: recreate the open-air reception courtyard of Donovan Hock's Bekenstein estate in Mass Effect 2: Kasumi — Stolen Memory, from the attached original environment artist frame. This single reference is the authority for all geometry, framing, colors and materials.
Preserve its two separate staircases exactly: a broad straight diagonal staircase running from near center-left to the far upper-left, and the narrower curved staircase on the right rising toward the upper center. Preserve their thin horizontal metal railings, the rounded stair plinths, the white curved building facade and dark blue-gray horizontal bands, central tall columns, recessed illuminated display at the back, the framed artwork on the right wall, the tall thin vertical poles at the left skyline, and the low mauve sunset seen through the open left side. Keep the circular cocktail table at the far lower-left, and keep the slim rope stanchions around the stairs. The original open floor between the stairs is the scene's empty standing space.
Composition: same camera position, direction and perspective as the reference, moderately low, wide landscape. The two staircase silhouettes and the view between them are essential; do not mirror them or merge them into a grand central staircase. Retain the reference's room proportions. If fitting the output aspect reveals slightly more near floor, continue only the floor panels already visible; do not add a new fighting platform, change the railings, flatten stairs or redesign the venue. Remove only the distant small guest silhouettes and the editor axis widget at bottom left. Preserve the sunset, wall artwork, table, original architecture and materials.
Style and lighting: faithful detailed real-time Mass Effect 2 environment rendering, smooth cream walls, cool blue-gray trim, warm mauve and pink sunset, restrained lens glow and soft shadows. Do not introduce stronger orange lighting, vegetation, a city panorama not visible in this frame, extra columns or a starship.
Output exactly one complete empty environment, no people, aliens, weapons, HUD, annotations, game title, logos, watermark, border, collage or multipanel. Opaque full-frame image.
jobs.productionNote: La référence du hall à escaliers ne correspond pas à la variante « Extérieur de la réception ». R0 conservé, jamais sélectionné pour la fiche finale.

jobs.subject: Eden Prime — spatioport
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one opaque landscape environment master for a Mass Effect stage prototype.
Primary request: reconstruct the exact beacon platform at Eden Prime's spaceport in the ORIGINAL 2007 Mass Effect, using the supplied in-game screenshot as the sole composition and architecture authority. Remove Commander Shepard and all game HUD/interface elements, exposing the same existing empty deck behind them. This is the original red-sky scene, not the warmer orange Legendary Edition relighting and not the ME3 From Ashes revisit.
Keep the reference camera direction, height, perspective and framing. Preserve the broad pinkish-brown rectangular metal floor panels with pairs of dark inset grooves running into depth, the low safety rail across the back, the segmented grated strip immediately behind the deck, the patches of dark grass outside the railing, the dark narrow distant industrial tower left of center, the low ruined structures and the red-brown smoke-filled sky. At right retain the exact Prothean beacon: its dark split foot braced on the deck, the thin blue-cyan arc just above its base and its tall thin upright artifact, still cut off by the top edge exactly as in the source. Keep the existing sloping pale industrial structure behind it and the tall dark ribbed building cropped at the far right.
Only fill the small floor area formerly occluded by the player and HUD by continuing its already visible repeating panels and seams. Do not change the camera to reveal more of the beacon, do not center it, enlarge it, remove it or move it. Do not add a new platform, buildings, a large space ship, Sovereign, more artifacts, flames or a new skyline. Preserve the visibly open original platform and existing railings.
Style: original Mass Effect real-time 3D environment language and reference palette, dark red hazy sky, warm reflected light on worn metal, sparse cool cyan at the artifact. Respect the source's modest detail: use restrained material textures, not invented elaborate surface ornament. No reinterpretation as a modern photoreal city. Maintain the source's simple material organization and scale.
Output exactly one empty full-frame landscape environment, without characters, weapons, drones, text, HUD, captions, labels, logos, border or collage. Opaque image.
jobs.productionNote: Les arcs cyan du réticule d’interaction ont été interprétés à tort comme une lumière physique. R0 conservé ; correction ciblée du seul fragment HUD en R1.

jobs.subject: Citadelle — tour du Conseil
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one opaque landscape environment master for a Mass Effect stage prototype.
Primary request: faithfully reconstruct the Citadel Council Chamber from the ORIGINAL Mass Effect (2007), matching the supplied in-game cinematic capture. This exact reference is the authority for camera, room layout, illumination and materials. Remove only the people standing on the near right balcony and any tiny distant people; fill their small silhouettes using the existing visible floor and wall surfaces.
Preserve this specific high oblique camera looking across the chamber. At lower right keep the small raised balcony with its dark thin railing and pale outer wall, pointing toward the central chamber; keep its actual limited dimensions. Preserve the translucent floor grid below, through which several small pink-leaved ornamental trees are visible; its dark thick crossing floor beams and the curved far floor edge. Keep the upper-left wall of tall vertical window divisions glowing lavender-white, the silhouetted tall dark trees behind the upper-left railing, the broad pale curved horizontal wall on the right, its dark recessed strip and large vertical structural members, the little warm light at the mid-right corner, and the subdued blue-lavender and gray atmosphere. Do not substitute the ME3 Council chamber or an enormous generic senate auditorium.
Composition: match the input framing and proportions, landscape. Do not flatten the chamber into a side-on arena or enlarge the balcony into a new combat platform. Do not rotate the viewpoint, add a central throne, council desks, a central energy machine, new stairs or new columns. Retain exactly the architectural forms and floor grid visible in the reference. This is an architectural background master; the source camera and the tiered layout take priority over making a gameplay lane.
Style: faithful restrained original Mass Effect real-time environment rendering. Preserve the soft violet light, cool gray metal, translucent blue floor and pink foliage. Improve clarity only enough to read the existing large forms; keep small material detail restrained because the reference is low-detail. No decorative reinvention or invented technological panels. Opaque full-frame scene.
Output exactly one complete empty environment, no people or aliens, weapons, HUD, text labels, captions, logos, border, split panels or collage.

jobs.subject: Bekenstein — propriété de Hock, balcon extérieur de la réception
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one opaque landscape environment master for a Mass Effect stage prototype.
Primary request: precisely reconstruct the EXTERIOR BALCONY behind the reception at Donovan Hock's estate on Bekenstein, from the original Mass Effect 2: Kasumi — Stolen Memory. The supplied screenshot from the Prima Games guide, figure 007, is the sole architecture, viewpoint, material and lighting authority. This scene is the exterior balcony and pool, not the interior reception hall and not the vault.
Match the reference composition exactly. Preserve the broad pale curved canopy sweeping overhead from upper left toward upper right, its thin tension lines, the dark support post at the far left, and the near low white-and-dark balcony parapet running diagonally from lower left toward the middle. Keep the square shallow reflecting pool at center-right below the camera, its thick beveled pale rim, the single round pale pool light near the front, the surrounding tan deck, the curved low bench/railing at the pool's left side and the simple low white parapet beyond. Beyond the terrace retain the dark rocky ridges and the flat-topped plateau on the left, the low cloud or mist between the hills, the myriad small city lights in the valley and the thin vertical distant skyline under a muted blue and mauve sunset. The skyline must remain distant and small, with the same silhouette proportions as the source, not a giant neon city wall.
Keep the same elevated three-quarter viewpoint, slightly above the reflecting pool. Remove Shepard and the guests, and remove the small Datapad HUD label at the top. Fill only their former silhouettes with the already visible pool water, deck panels, bench, low parapet and landscape. Do not introduce a new bridge, a horizontal fighting platform, new stairs, decorative plantings, sculpture, new pool shape, a second pool, ships or planets. Do not flatten or move the pool to invent an arena. The original exterior layout takes priority over a playable lane.
Style: detailed but restrained original Mass Effect 2 real-time game environment, preserve the warm pale white and tan architecture, lavender-pink reflections on the water, cool distant blue atmosphere and backlit haze. Keep the reference's dusk exposure and sun direction. Clarify existing forms without inventing ornate architectural details.
Output exactly one complete empty exterior stage-background master, landscape, opaque full frame. No people, aliens, weapons, HUD, labels, captions, game logos, watermark, frame, collage or multiple views.

jobs.subject: Eden Prime — retrait du réticule d’interaction
jobs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the edit target: the existing Eden Prime stage master. Make one localized correction only.
Remove the two bright cyan curved arcs on either side of the lower upright beacon, just above its dark foot at the right side of the scene. Those arcs are a retained interaction HUD reticle, not physical lights on the artifact. Replace just those two narrow cyan strokes and their immediate glow with the same unlit dark metal or background already surrounding them. Leave the actual dark beacon body, both feet and its vertical shaft completely unchanged.
Preserve every other feature of the target: exact framing, image dimensions/aspect ratio, camera perspective, metal floor pattern and printed floor marking, rear rail, red smoky sky, distant tower, hills, right building, overall color and exposure. Do not redesign the beacon, add luminous circuitry, reconstruct a different base, change the architecture, move any object, reframe, sharpen the whole image or change the lighting. No people, text overlays, labels or additional effects. Return the same opaque landscape environment with only the cyan HUD arcs removed.
